skill.name: Evidence-Based Verification Skill
skill.description: Collects verifiable test, build, quality, and deployment evidence before a task is marked complete.
skill.summary: Evidence-first templates and workflows for reliable software delivery.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: Manual review found an evidence-collection guide and static Markdown/JSON examples. All 17 detections are false positives caused by backticked code identifiers, documentation placeholders, sample output, and the missing YAML frontmatter. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or executable malicious behavior was found.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md does not use valid YAML frontmatter, which prevented static scanning.
remediation.suggestion: Add valid YAML frontmatter that declares the skill name, version, and description so automated scanners can process the file.

remediation.issue: Command placeholders and command examples can be mistaken for executable shell content by scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label all command text as documentation examples and keep placeholders in dedicated fenced Markdown blocks.

content.value_statement: Teams can mark work complete without reliable proof that it works. This skill provides workflows and templates to capture tests, builds, quality checks, and deployment evidence.
actual_capabilities: Guides collection of test results, exit codes, coverage, and run times.
Provides build-evidence templates for artifacts, warnings, errors, and timestamps.
Supplies checklists for linting, type checking, security scans, and deployment validation.
Defines minimum, production-grade, and gold-standard verification criteria.
Shows example reports for successful and failed test or build runs.
limitations: It provides guidance and templates; it does not run commands automatically.
It cannot prove a result is genuine without access to the underlying command output.
Coverage targets and quality thresholds require adaptation to each project.
Deployment health checks require project-specific endpoints and access.

use_cases.title: Confirm a feature before handoff
use_cases.description: Capture test, build, lint, and type-check evidence before handing a completed feature to a reviewer.

use_cases.title: Review pull requests with proof
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to request clear verification results for changed code and edge cases.

use_cases.title: Document a deployment
use_cases.description: Record pre-deployment checks, deployment output, health checks, and rollback readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic evidence report
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a task completion evidence report. I ran [command] and got exit code [code]. Include the result, timestamp, and next step.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a completed feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a verification checklist for this feature: [description]. Include relevant tests, build checks, linting, and type checking.

prompt_templates.title: Assess failed evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this failed verification output: [output]. Summarize what failed, list evidence, and propose the next verification steps. Do not mark the task complete.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare deployment evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a production deployment evidence report for [service]. Include pre-deployment checks, deployment results, health checks, smoke tests, and rollback verification.

output_examples.input: Document a successful test run with 24 passing tests and 87.5% coverage.
output: Test evidence records the command, exit code 0, duration, 24 passing tests, and 87.5% coverage.
The report includes a timestamp and states that the test requirement passed.

output_examples.input: Summarize a build that failed with three type errors.
output: Build evidence records a non-zero exit code, the three errors, and no artifacts.
The conclusion states that the task is not complete and requires fixes before another build.

best_practices: Run relevant verification after the latest code change, not only before it.
Record the exact command, exit code, timestamp, and a concise output summary.
Treat failed checks as blockers until evidence shows the issue is resolved.
anti_patterns: Do not claim tests passed without recorded command output or an exit code.
Do not mark work complete when a required build or test check fails.
Do not reuse old evidence after code or configuration changes.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflows and templates for documenting tests and other verification you run.

faq.question: What is the minimum evidence required?
faq.answer: Run at least one relevant verification, capture its exit code, record a timestamp, and store the evidence.

faq.question: Can I use it with Python, Rust, or Go?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance includes examples for several ecosystems and can be adapted to any project command.

faq.question: What should I do when a check fails?
faq.answer: Record the failure, identify the errors, fix them, and run the relevant verification again before completion.

faq.question: Does it require a coverage threshold?
faq.answer: It suggests thresholds, but your project team should set the appropriate standard.

faq.question: Can it help with deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides a deployment evidence workflow covering pre-checks, health checks, smoke tests, and rollback readiness.
